 Dallas Mavericks Brooklyn Nets Cooper Flagg and the Dallas Mavericks are off to a strong start in the 2026-27 season, going 5-4 through nine games and 5-2 when guard Kyrie Irving is in the lineup.
--> Cooper Flagg and the Dallas Mavericks are off to a strong start in the 2026-27 season, going 5-4 through nine games and 5-2 when guard Kyrie Irving is in the lineup.
 Irving is off the injury report and set to face his former team – the Brooklyn Nets – on Sunday.

 Brooklyn is playing the second night of a back-to-back, and it’s just 2-7 this season, ranking 22nd in net rating. The addition of Julius Randle has given Brooklyn a higher floor in the 2026-27 season, but this team is still expected to be one of the worst in the Eastern Conference.

 Cooper Flagg is well on his way to an All-Star berth in his second NBA season, and he’s looking to lead the Dallas Mavericks to a win over the Brooklyn Nets on Sunday.  
--> Cooper Flagg is well on his way to an All-Star berth in his second NBA season, and he’s looking to lead the Dallas Mavericks to a win over the Brooklyn Nets on Sunday.  
 Flagg is averaging 23.9 points, 6.8 rebounds and 6.4 assists per game this season, shooting 46.5 percent from the field. While Flagg isn’t averaging 14 or more rebounds and assists, I think he’s worth a shot in this market – especially at plus money – against this Brooklyn team.

 The Nets are one of the better teams in the league on the glass (eighth in rebound percentage), but they’re just 18th in opponent assists per game.

 Dallas comes into Sunday’s game against Brooklyn off a win against Utah, and it snapped a two-game skid after losses to Sacramento and San Antonio. 
--> Dallas comes into Sunday’s game against Brooklyn off a win against Utah, and it snapped a two-game skid after losses to Sacramento and San Antonio. 
 Dallas is just 18th in the league in net rating through the first few weeks of action, but it should be able to beat a Brooklyn team that is playing the second night of a back-to-back and is just 2-7 in the 2026-27 season, including a 1-4 record on the road.

 Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving have been pretty lethal as a duo this season, and the Mavs are 5-2 when Irving is in the lineup this season.
